entities.name: Silli-Adad
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Silli-Adad was the brief ruler of the ancient city-state of Larsa, in what is now southern Iraq, from circa 1835 BC to circa 1834 BC. He was a member of the Old Babylonian dynasty and his reign was marked by significant political instability.





Silli-Adad's rule was less than a full year, during which time he was removed from kingship and succeeded by Warad-Sin. The Larsa annals describe his removal as a result of his failure to secure key alliances with neighboring city-states.





Silli-Adad's legacy is largely one of political upheaval, and his brief reign serves as a reminder of the complexities and challenges of ruling in ancient Mesopotamia.
